title: all_vendors returns paginated vendor list with onboarding counters
preconditions: Buyer workspace has at least one BuyerSellerCompanyMapping in status active/invited/blacklisted; vendor Company is active. User has Company policy read access.
steps: 1. Authenticate as a buyer user of the workspace
2. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=1
3. Assert HTTP 200
4. Assert body carries total_pages, total_vendors, active_vendors, total_verified_vendors, total_unverified_vendors, total_in_progress_vendors, total_rejected_vendors
5. Assert every returned company id has a vendor_mapping_data entry
expectedResult: HTTP 200 rendering api/companies/all_companies. Companies ordered by name ASC. All four onboarding counters present and >= 0. No DB writes.
rationale: This is the primary vendor-master read; a regression here blanks the whole vendor module and the counters drive the onboarding tab badges.

title: all_vendors tab=rejected returns only rejected mappings
preconditions: Workspace vendor_onboarding_version is present. At least one BSM in status rejected and one in status active exist for this workspace.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors?tab=rejected&page=1
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert every returned company maps to a BSM with status rejected
4. Assert no active/invited/blacklisted vendor appears
expectedResult: HTTP 200. get_statuses_from_onboarding_tab resolves tab 'rejected' to REJECTED_STATUS only. Active vendors must be absent from the payload.
rationale: Tab-to-status mapping is a switch statement with per-tab branches; a wrong branch silently exposes rejected or active vendors in the wrong tab.

title: all_vendors with garbage tab falls back to default statuses without error
preconditions: Workspace has vendor_onboarding_version set and at least one active vendor.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors with an unknown tab value
2. Assert HTTP 200 and no exception
expectedResult: HTTP 200. get_statuses_from_onboarding_tab hits the else branch and returns DEFAULT_BSM_STATUSES = [:active, :invited, :blacklisted]. No 500, no empty-body crash.
rationale: Unknown enum values arriving from a stale frontend build must degrade to a safe default rather than raising.

title: all_vendors page=0 is coerced to page 1
preconditions: Workspace has more vendors than one page.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=1 and record the company id list
2. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=0
3. Compare the id lists
expectedResult: HTTP 200. Api::CompaniesController#paginate sets @page_number = 1 and only overrides when params['page'].to_i > 0, so page=0 returns exactly the page-1 result set.
rationale: Off-by-one/negative page handling is a classic source of Kaminari OFFSET errors and of clients silently re-rendering page 1 as if it were page 0.

title: all_vendors far-out page number returns an empty page, not a 500
preconditions: Workspace has fewer than 999999 pages of vendors.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=999999
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert companies list is empty and total_pages still reflects the real page count
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with an empty companies array. total_vendors/total_pages remain the real values. companies.total_pages must not raise.
rationale: Pagination abuse should cost a cheap empty page; a NoMethodError on total_pages for an empty relation is a real crash mode.

title: all_vendors Excel export with zero matching vendors is refused with code 494
preconditions: Apply a filter set that matches no vendor for this workspace.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors with download_excel=true and a filter matching nothing
2. Assert the request is rejected before any report generation
3. Assert no report_url is returned
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 494 'No Vendors found.' download_vendors_sheet and get_signed_url are never invoked; no S3 object is written.
rationale: Export paths run heavy workers and sign URLs; the empty-result guard must fire before any of that.

title: vendorlist_filtered without query param is rejected with code 2
preconditions: Authenticated buyer user with Company policy read access.
steps: 1. GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with no query parameter
2. Assert rejection before any DB search runs
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (render_error_json(2) fires on `unless query_string`). No companies/tags keys in the body.
rationale: A missing required query param must be a deterministic 422, not an unbounded ILIKE scan across the whole vendor master.

title: vendorlist_filtered matches name/email/vendor_code and paginates at 10 per page
preconditions: Workspace has a vendor whose company name, email or BSM vendor_code contains a known substring.
steps: 1. GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with a query and page=1
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert companies, tags, total_count and total_pages are present
4. Assert companies length <= 10
expectedResult: HTTP 200. The ILIKE runs over companies.name, companies.email and buyer_seller_company_mappings.vendor_code as a single bound :query. Page size is fixed at 10. total_pages is never 0.
rationale: This endpoint feeds the RFQ vendor-picker; both the three-column search and the never-zero total_pages guard are contract details the UI depends on.

title: vendorlist_filtered SQL-injection payload is bound, not interpolated
preconditions: Authenticated buyer user.
steps: 1. GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with query set to a SQL-injection payload
2. Assert HTTP 200 with an empty companies list
3. Assert buyer_seller_company_mappings and companies tables are intact afterwards
expectedResult: HTTP 200, zero or normal matches. The query reaches Postgres as the bound parameter in an ILIKE; no rows are returned by a tautology and no statement error is raised.
rationale: The one raw-SQL fragment in this action mixes three columns; verifying the bind survives refactors is cheaper than an incident.

title: vendorlist_filtered never returns another buyer's vendor mappings
preconditions: Two buyer workspaces A and B. Vendor V is mapped to workspace B only. Authenticate as a user of workspace A.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with vendor V's name
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert vendor V is absent from companies and from every tag's taggable_companies
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with vendor V absent. The base relation filters client_company_id: Current.workspace.id, so vendor V cannot surface.
rationale: Vendor names, emails and vendor codes are commercially sensitive; tenant leakage here is a breach, not a bug.

title: index returns columns and rows for a mapped vendor
preconditions: Config is_vendor_entity_mapping_enabled is ON. A BSM exists with dealing_with_company_id = {{vendorCompanyId}}.
steps: 1. GET /vendor_entity_mappings?dealing_with_company_id={{vendorCompanyId}}
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert body is {success:true, data:{columns:[...], rows:[...]}}
4. Assert each row carries entity_key, entity_name, vendor_code, erp_synced
expectedResult: HTTP 200. Rows are scoped by BOTH bsm_id and company_id = Current.workspace.id. columns comes from CustomConfiguration vendor_entity_mapping_columns, defaulting to []. No DB writes, no ERP dispatch.
rationale: The grid contract is what the entity-mapping screen renders; a serializer change breaks it silently.

title: index without dealing_with_company_id returns 400
preconditions: Config is_vendor_entity_mapping_enabled is ON.
steps: 1. GET /vendor_entity_mappings with no query string
2. Assert HTTP 400 and that the policy check never ran
expectedResult: HTTP 400 with body {error: 'dealing_with_company_id is required'}. The before_action set_bsm halts the chain before authorize, so this is a plain 400 and not the Pundit 455 path.
rationale: The first rung of the 400/404/422 ladder; it proves the guard is a before_action, which determines the code returned when the param is missing AND the flag is off.

title: index with an unknown dealing_with_company_id returns 404
preconditions: Config is_vendor_entity_mapping_enabled is ON. No BSM exists for id 999999999 in this workspace.
steps: 1. GET /vendor_entity_mappings?dealing_with_company_id=999999999
2. Assert HTTP 404
3. Assert the response contains no mapping rows
expectedResult: HTTP 404 with body {error: 'Vendor mapping not found'} from set_bsm when find_by returns nil.
rationale: Second rung of the ladder; a 200-with-empty-rows here would let a client believe an unmapped vendor exists and is simply un-synced.

title: index cannot read another buyer's vendor entity mappings
preconditions: Config ON in both workspaces. Vendor is mapped to workspace B. Authenticate as a workspace-A user with no BSM to that vendor.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, GET /vendor_entity_mappings for that vendor
2. Assert HTTP 404
3. Assert no entity_key, entity_name or vendor_code from workspace B appears
expectedResult: HTTP 404 {error: 'Vendor mapping not found'}. set_bsm filters on client_company_id: Current.workspace.id, so workspace B's BSM is invisible. Zero rows leak.
rationale: vendor_code is the ERP identity of a supplier; cross-tenant read here would expose a competitor's supplier codes.

title: index with the feature flag OFF is refused by policy with code 455
preconditions: CustomConfiguration is_vendor_entity_mapping_enabled is absent or falsy for the workspace. A valid BSM exists.
steps: 1. Confirm is_vendor_entity_mapping_enabled is OFF for the workspace
2. GET /vendor_entity_mappings for a valid vendor
3. Assert the request is refused and no rows are returned
expectedResult: VendorEntityMappingPolicy#index? returns falsy, Pundit::NotAuthorizedError is raised and rescued, producing HTTP 422 with error.code 455. No mapping rows in the body.
rationale: Config-gated modules must fail closed; a policy that returns nil instead of raising would leak the whole grid to non-licensed tenants.

title: unmapped excludes entity keys already mapped to this vendor
preconditions: Config ON. WidgetDataMapping rows with key='vendor_entity_mapping' exist. At least one value is already mapped for this bsm_id.
steps: 1. GET the index and record the mapped entity_key set
2. GET /vendor_entity_mappings/unmapped for the same vendor
3. Assert HTTP 200 and body {success:true, data:[{display_value, value}]}
4. Assert the intersection of the two sets is empty
expectedResult: HTTP 200. Candidates come from WidgetDataMapping(key: 'vendor_entity_mapping', company_id: workspace, status: active) minus the mapped_keys set built from VendorEntityMapping.where(bsm_id:).
rationale: This list is the dropdown that drives creation; a stale entry is how users trigger the duplicate-422 path and redundant ERP calls.

title: unmapped without dealing_with_company_id returns 400
preconditions: Config is_vendor_entity_mapping_enabled ON.
steps: 1. GET /vendor_entity_mappings/unmapped with no query string
2. Assert HTTP 400
expectedResult: HTTP 400 {error: 'dealing_with_company_id is required'} from the shared set_bsm before_action, which also guards the unmapped action.
rationale: The unmapped action is registered via a separate route scope; it is easy to add a new action there and forget it inherits set_bsm.

title: unmapped with an unknown vendor id returns 404 and not an empty 200
preconditions: Config ON. No BSM for id 999999999 in this workspace.
steps: 1. GET /vendor_entity_mappings/unmapped?dealing_with_company_id=999999999
2. Assert HTTP 404
expectedResult: HTTP 404 {error: 'Vendor mapping not found'}. The WidgetDataMapping query must never run for a non-existent BSM.
rationale: Returning the full entity catalogue for a non-existent vendor would let any caller enumerate a tenant's ERP subsidiary keys.

title: create with blank entity_key is rejected with 400 before any ERP dispatch
preconditions: Config ON. Valid BSM for {{vendorCompanyId}}. Outbound integration templates may exist - they must not be invoked.
steps: 1. POST /vendor_entity_mappings with entity_key set to an empty string
2. Assert HTTP 400
3. Assert no outbound dispatch record was created
4. Assert vendor_entity_mappings row count is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 400 {error: 'entity_key is required'}. Integrations::OutboundDispatcherService.dispatch_sync is never called and no VendorEntityMapping row is created.
rationale: This is the safe half of the create ladder: it must reject strictly before the synchronous ERP call, otherwise a QA run fires real supplier-creation requests at the customer's SAP.

title: create with an entity_key absent from WidgetDataMapping returns 404 before dispatch
preconditions: Config ON. Valid BSM. No active WidgetDataMapping row matches the payload value.
steps: 1. POST /vendor_entity_mappings with an entity_key that exists in no WidgetDataMapping row
2. Assert HTTP 404
3. Assert no outbound integration was dispatched
4. Assert no row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 404 {error: 'Entity not found in mapping configuration'}. The lookup is scoped by key, value, company_id and status: active. dispatch_sync is not reached.
rationale: Second rung of the create ladder and the guard that stops an arbitrary attacker-supplied subsidiary_key from being forwarded into the ERP payload.

title: create with an injection payload as entity_key is refused without crashing
preconditions: Config ON. Valid BSM for {{vendorCompanyId}}.
steps: 1. POST /vendor_entity_mappings with a SQL/script payload as entity_key
2. Assert HTTP 404 (or 400 if the payload strips to blank) and never a 5xx
3. Assert widget_data_mappings and vendor_entity_mappings tables are intact
4. Assert no ERP dispatch occurred
expectedResult: HTTP 404 'Entity not found in mapping configuration'. The sanitize_input_params filter strips HTML first; the remainder is passed as a bound value to find_by. No table dropped, no dispatch_sync call, no row created.
rationale: entity_key is echoed into the outbound ERP payload as subsidiary_key, so it is the highest-value injection sink in this controller.

title: create with a non-existent vendor id returns 404 from set_bsm, never reaching entity validation
preconditions: Config ON. No BSM for id 999999999 in this workspace.
steps: 1. POST /vendor_entity_mappings with dealing_with_company_id=999999999 and a valid-looking entity_key
2. Assert HTTP 404 'Vendor mapping not found' (not 'Entity not found in mapping configuration')
3. Assert no ERP dispatch
expectedResult: HTTP 404 with the set_bsm message 'Vendor mapping not found'. Distinguishing the two 404 messages proves the vendor-scope check precedes the entity-catalogue check.
rationale: Two different 404s share a status code; asserting on the message proves the ordering, which is what prevents catalogue enumeration.

title: PR list page 1 returns the documented envelope
preconditions: Workspace has at least one PurchaseRequest not in status in_active with line items.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with page=1 and a status filter
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert keys purchase_requests, total_pages, total_pr_count, columns_configuration, closure_configuration
4. Assert each purchase_request carries rfq_no and a line_items array with the four quantity fields
expectedResult: HTTP 200 from PurchaseRequests::ViewService. Default page size is 50. closure_configuration mirrors CustomConfiguration is_pr_partial_closure_enabled. No DB writes.
rationale: The list envelope drives the whole PR grid plus the partial-closure button visibility; contract drift breaks both at once.

title: PR list page=0 collapses to page 1
preconditions: Workspace has more than 50 PR line items so page 1 and page 2 differ.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 and record the PR uuid list
2. GET /purchase_requests?page=0
3. Assert both return the same first-page payload
expectedResult: HTTP 200. PurchaseRequests::SearchQuery sets @page = [1, params[:page].to_i].max, so 0, negative and non-numeric all resolve to page 1.
rationale: Silent page coercion is correct behaviour here, but it must be verified rather than assumed - a change to .to_i handling would produce a negative OFFSET.

title: PR list far-out page returns an empty page with a real total_pages
preconditions: Workspace has fewer than 999999 pages of PR items.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=999999 with a status filter
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert purchase_requests is empty
4. Assert total_pages and total_pr_count still describe the full result set
expectedResult: HTTP 200, empty purchase_requests. Kaminari yields an empty relation; total_pages must remain the true page count.
rationale: Pagination abuse must not turn into an expensive COUNT storm or a nil-dereference in the serializer chain.

title: ageing_status=breach returns only items aged at or beyond the breach threshold
preconditions: Config purchase_request_ageing_enabled is ON. Workspace has PR items older than 7 days with no PO, plus items younger than 4 days.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with ageing_status breach
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert every returned line item reports ageing_in_days >= 7
4. Assert items younger than 4 days are absent
expectedResult: HTTP 200. filter_by_ageing_status applies AGEING_DAYS_EXPR >= AGEING_BREACH_THRESHOLD (7). 'warning' is the 4..6 band.
rationale: Ageing days are computed by a hand-written SQL expression; thresholds 4 and 7 are the SLA the business reports on.

title: Unrecognised ageing_status value is ignored instead of erroring
preconditions: Config purchase_request_ageing_enabled is ON.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with an unknown ageing_status value
2. Assert HTTP 200 and a result set equal to the unfiltered active list
expectedResult: HTTP 200. The case/else branch logs 'Unrecognized filter' and adds no condition, so the original relation is returned unfiltered.
rationale: An unknown filter that silently widens results is safer than a 500, but the tester must confirm which of the two the code actually does.

title: is_dormant filter returns only PRs past the dormant threshold and not yet unlocked
preconditions: Config pr_dormant_threshold_days has a value > 0. Workspace has a PR older than the threshold with dormant_unlocked_at NULL, one newer PR, and one already unlocked.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with is_dormant true
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert the old locked PR is present
4. Assert the newer PR and the already-unlocked PR are absent
expectedResult: HTTP 200. The scope dormant_locked_for_company requires status active, dormant_unlocked_at IS NULL and CURRENT_DATE - created_at::date >= threshold.
rationale: Dormant locking gates PR usability for buyers; both the unlock timestamp and the >= threshold boundary must be exercised or an unlocked PR stays hidden forever.

title: is_dormant filter is a no-op when the dormant feature is not configured
preconditions: CustomConfiguration pr_dormant_threshold_days is absent, or its value is 0.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with only a status filter and record the PR ids
2. GET the same URL with is_dormant true added
3. Assert both responses are HTTP 200 with identical PR id sets
expectedResult: HTTP 200 identical to the unfiltered call. filter_by_dormant_status returns the untouched relation when dormant_feature_enabled_for? is false, so the scope - whose SQL would bind a nil threshold - is never built.
rationale: With the flag off the threshold is nil; without the guard the scope would compare against NULL and quietly return zero PRs, emptying the grid for every un-configured tenant.

title: PR list cannot be steered to another company's PRs via pr_ids
preconditions: Two workspaces A and B. A PR belongs to workspace B. Authenticate as a workspace-A user.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, GET /purchase_requests filtered by a PR id from workspace B
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert purchase_requests is empty and total_pr_count is 0
4. Assert no rfq_no or line item from that PR appears
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with an empty result. The base relation is scoped for_companies([Current.workspace.id]) and the pr_ids scope only narrows it further - it can never widen it.
rationale: has_scope filters run on top of the tenant scope; an accidental reorder that applies pr_ids to an unscoped relation is exactly how cross-tenant PR leaks happen.

title: Injection payload in the rfq_no filter is escaped by sql_like
preconditions: Authenticated buyer user with at least one PR in the workspace.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with an injection payload in the rfq_no filter
2. Assert HTTP 200 and an empty or normally-filtered result
3. Assert the purchase_requests table is intact
expectedResult: HTTP 200, no rows matched by the tautology. The scopes route the value through PurchaseRequest.sql_like before the ILIKE bind, so both the quote and the wildcard are neutralised.
rationale: Free-text PR number search is user-facing and reaches an ILIKE; sql_like escaping is the only thing standing between it and a wildcard-driven full scan.

title: Malformed filters JSON does not produce a 5xx
preconditions: Authenticated buyer user.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with a truncated filters JSON string
2. Assert the response is not a 5xx
3. Assert either a normal 200 envelope or a deterministic 4xx
expectedResult: No 500. create_filter_params delegates to CommonFunctions.parse_filters; a truncated JSON string must not escape as an unrescued JSON::ParserError to the client.
rationale: filters arrives as a raw JSON string and is parsed in at least two places; truncated query strings are routine in the wild and must not page the on-call.

title: PR detail returns line items, columns_configuration and closure_configuration
preconditions: PR {{prId}} belongs to the acting user's workspace and is visible through get_filtered_purchase_requests.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests/{{prId}}
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert the purchase_request object plus columns_configuration and closure_configuration keys
4. Assert line items exclude any item in status in_active
expectedResult: HTTP 200. purchase_request_items are filtered with where.not(status: :in_active); closure_configuration echoes is_pr_partial_closure_enabled so the UI can decide whether to offer partial closure. No writes.
rationale: The detail payload is assembled from a dozen preloaded maps; the highest-value assertion is that the quantity and configuration blocks travel together.

title: PR detail for a non-existent id is refused with code 2
preconditions: No PurchaseRequest with id 999999999 is visible to the acting user.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests/999999999
2. Assert the request is refused
3. Assert no PR fields are present in the body
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' from get_purchase_request_from_params, which returns [nil, 2] when the filtered relation has no match. The Pundit authorize call is never reached.
rationale: Procol deliberately returns the same generic code for missing and forbidden PRs; verifying it prevents a future 'helpful' 404 that would confirm the existence of other tenants' PRs.

title: PR detail with a garbage id fails closed without a 5xx
preconditions: Authenticated buyer user.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with a non-uuid junk id
2. Assert the response is not a 5xx
3. Assert error.code 2
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2. The global check_for_uuid before_action runs EncryptDecrypt.decode_data, which returns nil for undecodable input; params[:id] becomes nil and the lookup returns [nil, 2].
rationale: Every id in this API passes through a custom Base64 decoder that can return nil; the endpoint must treat that as 'not found' rather than querying with nil.

title: Empty line_items array is rejected with code 2
preconditions: Event group {{eventGroupUuid}} is a draft in the acting workspace.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/pri_to_draft_project with line_items set to an empty array
2. Assert rejection
3. Assert no EventGroupLineItem was created for the event group
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. The controller guard fires before PrToErfxService is constructed, so no transaction opens.
rationale: A blank submit must not open a transaction or touch PR quantities; the guard also covers three other failure modes that share this code.

title: Quantity above open quantity plus tolerance is rejected with 557
preconditions: Event group {{eventGroupUuid}} is draft and already has at least one line item. PR item {{prItemId}} is unlinked with a known quantity_open.
steps: 1. Read the item's quantity_open and the workspace over_quantity_tolerance_percentage
2. POST with a quantity far above the allowed maximum
3. Assert rejection with 557
4. Repeat at exactly the boundary and assert acceptance
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 557. validate_purchase_request_items_data computes max_allowed = quantity_open * (1 + tolerance / 100.0) and returns false when adding_quantity > max_allowed; the boundary value itself must pass.
rationale: Over-quantity sourcing means buying more than was requisitioned; the tolerance multiplier is float maths, so the exact boundary is where it breaks.

title: Undecodable event group uuid is refused with code 2
preconditions: Authenticated buyer user with draft-project creation rights.
steps: 1. POST to pri_to_draft_project with a junk event group uuid and a valid line_items array
2. Assert the response is not a 5xx
3. Assert error.code 2
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2. check_for_uuid runs decode_data on the non-integer id, which returns nil, so event_group resolves to nil and the blank guard fires. No transaction, no writes.
rationale: A mistyped or truncated uuid in a shared link must produce a clean 422 rather than an ActiveRecord type error inside a transaction.

title: Partial closure is blocked with 861 when the feature config is off or missing
preconditions: CustomConfiguration is_pr_partial_closure_enabled is absent or false for the workspace.
steps: 1. Confirm closure_configuration shows the feature as disabled
2. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with one valid item
3. Assert rejection
4. Assert quantity_closed, meta_data and Remark rows are unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 861 'Partial closure of purchase requests is disabled for your organization.' PartialClosureService#execute returns 861 before validate() runs.
rationale: 861 is the outermost gate; it must precede every other validation so an un-licensed tenant cannot even probe which item ids are valid.

title: More than 20 distinct items in one request is refused with 823
preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons. 21 distinct valid PR item ids are available.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with 21 distinct pr_item_ids
2. Assert rejection with 823
3. Repeat with exactly 20 and assert it passes the limit check
4. Assert nothing was closed in the 21-item attempt
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 823 'Cannot close more than 20 PR items at once.' MAX_ITEMS_PER_REQUEST is 20 and the check is length > MAX on the de-duplicated array, so 20 is allowed and 21 is not.
rationale: A hard batch cap protects a row-locking transaction; the > vs >= boundary decides whether the documented limit of 20 actually works.

title: Duplicate ids are de-duplicated before the 20-item cap is applied
preconditions: Feature ON. SAFETY: this case deliberately repeats a NON-EXISTENT id rather than a real open item, so it exercises the uniq-before-cap ordering without any risk of actually closing live PR data.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with the same non-existent id repeated 25 times
2. Assert the response is NOT 823 (proving uniq ran before the cap)
3. Assert it is 528 instead (id not found), i.e. the batch collapsed to a single id
expectedResult: Not 823 - expect 861 (feature off) or 528 (id not found). The constructor performs pr_item_ids.uniq before validate(), so 25 copies collapse to one id and the length check sees 1, never tripping the 20-item cap.
rationale: Order of uniq vs the cap decides whether a double-clicking UI hits a spurious 823. Using a bogus id proves the ordering without mutating real data.

title: Empty pr_item_ids is refused with code 2
preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with an empty pr_item_ids array
2. Assert rejection with code 2
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters', the first rung of validate() after the 861 feature gate.
rationale: Missing required payload must be caught before any query; a blank array reaching the item lookup would instead surface as a confusing 528.

title: closure_reason outside the configured reason keys is refused with code 2
preconditions: Feature ON with a known closure_reasons list. {{prItemId}} is a valid open item.
steps: 1. Read the allowed reason keys from closure_configuration
2. PATCH partial_close with a closure_reason absent from that list
3. Assert rejection
4. Assert the item's quantities and remarks are unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 with the explicit message 'Invalid closure reason'. allowed_closure_reason_keys is built from config['closure_reasons'] - an empty or missing list therefore rejects every reason.
rationale: The reason key is persisted into partial_closure_metadata and drives downstream reporting; accepting free text would poison the closure analytics permanently.

title: Blank remarks are refused with code 2
preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons. {{prItemId}} is a valid open item.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with remarks set to an empty string
2. Assert rejection
3. Assert no Remark row with event_type 'partial_closure' was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 with message 'Remarks are required'. The controller coerces params[:remarks].to_s, so a missing key becomes '' and is caught by the same blank? guard.
rationale: Remarks are the audit justification embedded in every generated Remark message; an empty value makes the closure trail worthless and is irreversible.

title: Non-existent item ids are refused with 528 and the batch is all-or-nothing
preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons. One valid open item plus one id that does not exist.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with one valid and one non-existent id
2. Assert rejection with 528
3. Assert the valid item was NOT partially closed
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 528 'item(s) not found'. When the fetched count differs from the requested count the whole batch is refused, so the good item stays untouched.
rationale: Partial-batch semantics matter: users must not discover that one of twenty items silently closed while the request reported an error.

title: Another company's PR item cannot be closed and returns the same 528
preconditions: Feature ON in workspace A. A PR item belongs to workspace B and is open. Authenticate as a workspace-A user.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, PATCH partial_close with the foreign item id
2. Assert HTTP 422 error.code 528 - identical to the not-found response
3. Re-read the item in workspace B and assert nothing changed
4. Assert no Remark row was written
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 528 with zero writes. The item scope filters purchase_requests.company_id, so a foreign item never loads and the count mismatch triggers 528 - the same code as a non-existent id, giving no existence signal.
rationale: Closing another tenant's PR item is a destructive cross-tenant write; the count-mismatch guard is the only barrier and it must also not disclose that the id exists.

title: An already partially-closed item is refused with 863
preconditions: Feature ON. {{prItemId}} has already been partially closed once.
steps: 1. Confirm the item already carries partial_closure_metadata
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 863
4. Assert quantity_closed did not change and no second Remark was added
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 863 'One or more items have already been partially closed.' The guard runs after the 528 existence check and before item classification, so it wins over 862/868/867.
rationale: Re-closing would overwrite the original partial_closure_metadata - destroying the first closure's reason, remarks and closer identity with no way back.

title: An item with neither open nor in-progress quantity is refused with 862
preconditions: Feature ON. {{prItemId}} has quantity_open = 0 AND quantity_in_progress = 0 and is not yet partially closed.
steps: 1. Confirm both quantities are 0
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 862
4. Assert no quantity or metadata change
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 862 'Items cannot be closed as they have no open quantity.' classify_items buckets by quantity_open > 0, then quantity_in_progress > 0, else no_closable_qty; any member of that last bucket fails the whole batch.
rationale: Closing a zero-quantity item would write metadata claiming a closure of 0 - noise in the audit trail that also permanently blocks the item via 863.

title: In-progress-only item in an event group with no generated order is refused with 868
preconditions: Feature ON. The company has PO integration enabled. {{prItemId}} has quantity_open = 0, quantity_in_progress > 0, and its event group has NO generated order.
steps: 1. Confirm the item is in-progress only and its event group has no generated order
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 868
4. Control: repeat where PO integration is OFF and assert 868 does NOT fire
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 868 'In-progress items cannot be closed because no order has been generated from the sourcing event'. The whole check is gated on @company.is_po_integration_enabled?.
rationale: 868 is conditional on a per-company integration flag - the most likely place for a false rejection on non-integrated tenants, so the negative control matters as much as the positive case.

title: In-progress item with a pending reorder request is refused with 867
preconditions: Feature ON. {{prItemId}} is in-progress only, its event group HAS a generated order, and an active ItemReorderRequest exists with new_order_id NULL.
steps: 1. Confirm the active reorder request with a null new_order_id
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 867
4. Control: resolve the reorder and assert 867 no longer fires
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 867 'Item cannot be closed because a reorder request is pending for it.' The check runs after 868 within the in-progress branch, so ordering between the two codes must be preserved.
rationale: Closing an item under an open reorder would strand the reorder workflow with no PR to attach to; the 868-then-867 ordering is what a regression would silently flip.

title: Hostile pr_item_ids and attachments payloads must not produce a 5xx
preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with pr_item_ids as a scalar injection string and attachments as bare strings including a malformed URI
2. Assert the response is a deterministic 4xx and never a 5xx
3. Assert the tables are intact
4. Assert no partial_closure_metadata was written
expectedResult: A 4xx (422 with code 528 or 2), never a 500. The controller wraps both fields in Array(); normalize_attachments coerces non-hash entries and rescues URI::InvalidURIError; item ids reach ActiveRecord as bound values.
rationale: attachments is the one field parsed with URI.parse and File.basename on user input, and pr_item_ids is the one array reaching a locking UPDATE - both deserve an explicit fuzz case.
